$header_note: QPB v1.5.7 Test 2 — Mac ship-readiness acceptance. 7-run matrix exercising runner × tier × channel (pip-local-wheel + npm-local-tgz) with a pool=2 copilot exercise. Capable models only (no deliberate weakening). Pools: claude=3 (haiku+sonnet+opus parallel), codex=2, copilot=2. All expects permissive on gate_result + tight on observability assertions. The point is to validate that v1.5.7's channel + runner infrastructure works under production-like conditions across the matrix — NOT to predict capability outcomes.

runs.description: Cheap-tier smoke check: claude/haiku reviews gson via pip-local-wheel (Mode A). Exercises the claude runner + pip channel with the lowest-cost model. Permissive gate_result expect.
Mid-tier: claude/sonnet reviews Express via npm-local-tgz (Mode A). Exercises the claude runner + npm channel — different repo + different channel + different tier from row 1.
Top-tier: claude/opus reviews Ory Keto via pip-local-wheel (Mode A). Largest repo in the matrix; capable model exercises the full pipeline against a complex Go codebase.

Capable codex: gpt-5.4-codex reviews chi via npm-local-tgz (Mode B). Mode B is the production pattern for codex (run_playbook drives one phase per fresh invocation). Validates 150's npx --yes fix end-to-end with a capable model — install should finish in seconds.
Capable codex on the other channel: gpt-5.4-codex reviews gson via pip-local-wheel (Mode B). Same model + different channel from row 4 — pins the channel-vs-runner orthogonality.

Copilot capable on pip-local-wheel: gpt-5.4 reviews Express. First of the two copilot runs designed to exercise pool=2. Validates 145 witness fallback + 148 install.log banner fallback in production conditions.

Copilot capable on npm-local-tgz: gpt-5.4 reviews chi. Second of the two copilot runs — same model + different channel + different repo from row 5. With pool=2, this and row 5 should run concurrently — pins 125's per-runner concurrency cap.
